question: Which year was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** was launched on **28th August 2014** by the Government of India. It is a national-level initiative aimed at achieving comprehensive financial inclusion.
 
• The scheme was launched under the leadership of the Prime Minister of India, **Narendra Modi**, with the vision of ensuring access to financial services such as bank accounts, credit, insurance, and pensions for all households in India.
 
• The scheme is particularly targeted at the economically weaker sections of society, who previously lacked access to banking and financial services. *Hence, the correct year is 2014.*
 
• It was launched with the aim to eliminate financial exclusion and provide basic financial services like savings accounts, credit, insurance, pension, and financial literacy.
 
• The scheme is regarded as one of the largest financial inclusion initiatives in the world and was recognized by the **Guinness World Records** for opening the highest number of bank accounts in a single week.
 
• Under the PMJDY, individuals receive a **zero-balance savings account**, a **RuPay debit card**, and an accidental insurance cover of **Rs. 1 lakh**. The overdraft facility of **Rs. 5,000** is available after six months of satisfactory operation of the account.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of PMJDY:**

 
 
• To provide universal access to banking facilities for every household in the country, especially in rural and remote areas, ensuring no one is excluded from the banking ecosystem.
 
• To offer basic banking accounts with overdraft facilities for every household, thereby promoting savings habits and financial literacy.
 
• To integrate individuals with the formal financial system, enabling them to access credit facilities, insurance, and pension services.
 
 
 
• **Features of PMJDY:**
 
 
• Accounts opened under PMJDY are zero-balance accounts, meaning account holders are not required to maintain a minimum balance.
 
• The scheme provides access to **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**, ensuring government benefits such as subsidies and pensions are directly credited to beneficiaries' accounts.
 
• The scheme includes a life insurance cover of **Rs. 30,000** for accounts opened before January 26, 2015.
 
• PMJDY also facilitates financial literacy programs to educate account holders about various financial products and services.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of PMJDY:**
 
 
• As of **2023**, over **50 crore bank accounts** have been opened under the scheme, with total deposits exceeding **Rs. 2 lakh crore**.
 
• A significant portion of the accounts opened under PMJDY belongs to women and individuals in rural areas, promoting gender equality and rural development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Recognition:**

 
 
• The PMJDY initiative has been recognized globally as one of the largest financial inclusion schemes in the world, significantly reducing financial exclusion in India.
 
 
 
• **Role of Technology:**
 
 
• The integration of technology, such as **Aadhaar** and mobile banking, has played a crucial role in the success of the scheme by simplifying processes and ensuring transparency.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Rural Areas:**
 
 
• The scheme has significantly improved the financial inclusion of rural households, enabling them to access formal banking systems and government benefits directly.
